chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) lifted Hasan and Husayn and said:

I seek refuge for you two with the complete words of Allah and all His good names, generally, from the evil of the venomous reptile and the insect, and from the evil of every envious eye, and from the evil of an envious person when he envies.
Then the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) turned to us and said: This is how Ibrahim used to seek refuge for Ismail and Ishaq (peace be upon them).

key_terms.أُعِيذُكُمَا: I seek refuge for you two

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication for seeking refuge (ta'widh) for children mentioned in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him) specific practice of seeking refuge (ta'widh) for his grandsons using Allah’s complete words and names, a tradition he explicitly links to Prophet Ibrahim’s protection of Ismail and Ishaq. In Shia scholarship, this narration underscores the spiritual authority of the Ahl al-Bayt and validates the use of Quranic verses and divine names as effective means of warding off the evil eye and envy. It serves as a foundational text for the practice of ruqyah within the family of the Prophet, emphasizing continuity with earlier prophetic traditions.
